extra_misconceptions.fact: Friction from rubbing or snow crystals shreds frozen tissue cells; warm frostbite gently in tepid water around 99 to 102 degrees.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rubbing frostbitten fingers or toes vigorously with snow restores circulation without damaging the frozen skin.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most sports concussions occur without loss of consciousness, and symptoms like dizziness or confusion may appear hours later.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A skateboarder who stands up immediately after hitting their head and never loses consciousness cannot have a concussion.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Snowboard helmets meet ASTM F2040 standards for cold-weather impacts and ear warmth, whereas skate helmets follow CPSC or ASTM F1492.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Multi-impact skate helmets protect just as well as certified snow helmets during high-speed collisions on icy ski slopes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cold air blunts the thirst response while dry altitude respiration accelerates fluid loss, so riders must hydrate on a set schedule.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Thirst is an early and reliable warning sign to start drinking water during high-altitude snowboarding in cold weather.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a rider's core temperature when wet cotton base layers remain against the skin in freezing wind?
Which physical indicator distinguishes life-threatening heatstroke from heat exhaustion during a summer skate session?
Why is it dangerous to allow a snowboarder with a suspected concussion to return to the slope that same afternoon?
What surface hazards must you clear or mark during a pre-ride walk-through of an outdoor concrete skatepark?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cold static stretching temporarily weakens muscle output; start with dynamic movements like lunges and leg swings to raise blood flow.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Holding deep static stretches for sixty seconds on cold muscles is the safest way to warm up before dropping into a halfpipe.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Skatepark flow runs on a turn-taking queue where only one rider occupies a bowl line at a time, regardless of skill level.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A faster, more experienced skater always has the right-of-way over beginners who are taking turns in a skatepark bowl.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dangling feet or boards over the coping blocks the grind surface and creates a severe collision hazard for riders coming up the wall.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sitting on the coping edge of a ramp with your feet dangling inside the transition is a safe way to wait for your turn.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Under the Responsibility Code, the person ahead has the right-of-way because their back is turned to uphill traffic on the heel edge.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Downhill snowboarders must constantly look uphill and yield to faster riders approaching from behind on the same trail.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a snowboarder position themselves if they must stop on a trail, and why are blind rollovers off-limits?
Under what condition does an uphill rider have the right-of-way over a downhill rider on an open mountain run?
What happens to explosive jump power and joint stability when you perform long static stretches on cold muscles before riding?
Which visual cues confirm that the bowl or landing zone is completely clear before you drop in at a busy skatepark?

extra_misconceptions.fact: WD-40 is a solvent that strips factory grease and attracts dust; clean bearings with isopropyl alcohol and apply speed cream or skate oil.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Spraying household WD-40 into dirty skateboard bearings lubricates the steel balls for long-term high-speed rolling.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Over-cranking the kingpin crushes and splits the urethane bushings; install harder durometer bushings if you need stiffer truck response.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tightening a new skateboard kingpin nut until the urethane bushings bulge out is the proper way to stabilize loose trucks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wax belongs inside the microscopic pores of the sintered or extruded base, and excess surface wax actually creates drag until scraped off.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leaving a thick coat of unscraped hot wax on a snowboard base makes the board glide faster on cold morning snow.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Snowboard edges require a precise bevel guide of eighty-eight to ninety degrees and a diamond stone to remove burrs without gouging metal.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Filing both the base edge and side edge at random angles with a coarse hardware rasp keeps a snowboard sharp for ice.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to turn responsiveness and wheel-bite risk when you loosen a skateboard kingpin nut too far?
Which physical indicator on a skateboard bearing shield or axle nut tells you that the assembly needs cleaning or replacement?
Why is it dangerous to ride a snowboard with delaminated metal edges or loose binding baseplate screws on hardpack snow?
What measurement confirms that your snowboard binding stance width and highback forward lean match your natural leg anatomy?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Catching your full body weight on outstretched hands frequently snaps the radius or scaphoid bones; tuck your arms and roll onto fleshy areas.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Reaching out with locked arms and open palms is the safest reflex to stop a forward fall on concrete or hardpack snow.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Weighting the tail lifts the front contact points off the snow and prevents the sidecut from engaging, causing the board to wash out.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leaning backward onto your tail foot helps you initiate smoother, more controlled snowboard turns on steeper mountain slopes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Tail scraping wears down deck plies into "razor tail" and easily locks up; controlled foot braking with a flat sole is far more stable.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scraping the wooden tail of a skateboard on asphalt is the most reliable primary braking method at moderate downhill speeds.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Board stance depends on balance and lead-leg preference rather than handedness, and many right-handed athletes naturally ride goofy.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A rider who writes and kicks a ball with their right foot must always ride in a regular left-foot-forward board stance.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to edge hold on a snowboard or turn radius on a skateboard when your weight shifts backward onto your rear foot?
Why is it dangerous to push a skateboard with your front foot while keeping your back foot planted near the tail ("mongo")?
Where should a rider position their arms, chin, and forearms when absorbing a fall to prevent a wrist fracture or whiplash?
Which physical indicator shows the difference between a true carved turn on a clean snow edge and a skidded braking turn?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Freezing temperatures preserve food waste for months, attracting wildlife to ski runs and polluting spring snowmelt in alpine watersheds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tossing biodegradable fruit peels or food scraps off a chairlift is harmless because they decompose quickly under the snowpack.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Over-waxing public ledges or coping causes dangerously unpredictable slick spots for other riders and damages municipal concrete surfaces.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying paraffin candle wax to every concrete ledge in a community skatepark improves the park for all skaters and bikers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Park features change daily from grooming, freeze-thaw cycles, and heavy traffic, so every session requires a slow "look before you leap" lap.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hitting a terrain park jump on your first run without a scout lap is safe if you rode that same feature the day before.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ski patrollers perform daily trail sweeps, mark hazards, maintain rescue toboggans, and conduct avalanche control work before lifts open.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: National Ski Patrol members only rescue injured skiers and have no role in avalanche mitigation or slope hazard prevention.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition does an unmaintained kicker lip or rutted landing transition become unsafe for intermediate park maneuvers?
What happens to fragile alpine tundra vegetation and wildlife when snowboarders duck boundary ropes into closed winter terrain?
Which physical indicator in a terrain park tells you whether a feature is rated small, medium, or large before you hit it?
What certifications and outdoor emergency skills must a volunteer master to serve on the National Ski Patrol at a mountain?
